title: Life Without Sunlight
learning_objectives_vi: Theo dõi bài giảng học thuật có lập luận và ví dụ.
Hoàn thành ghi chú, tóm tắt hoặc bảng bằng đúng từ được nghe.
Nhận diện signposting và mối quan hệ giữa các ý.

turns.text_en: Most familiar ecosystems ultimately depend on sunlight. Yet some deep-sea communities live far below the reach of daylight, close to places where hot, mineral-rich fluids escape from the ocean floor. Their existence changed how biologists think about energy in ecosystems. Today's lecture explains what supports these organisms and why the habitats are difficult to study.
turns.meaning_vi: Bài giảng giới thiệu hệ sinh thái biển sâu sống nhờ hóa năng gần miệng phun thủy nhiệt.

turns.text_en: The first discovery of dense life around hot springs on the seabed surprised scientists who expected such dark environments to support only sparse communities. The organisms survive through relationships involving microbes, minerals and flowing water. Understanding these links requires measurements of the environment as well as inventories of the visible animals.
turns.meaning_vi: Mở rộng bối cảnh, giới thiệu vấn đề nghiên cứu.

turns.text_en: At a hydrothermal vent, heated water emerges through cracks in the seabed after interacting with hot rock. Some microbes obtain energy through chemosynthesis, using chemical reactions rather than sunlight to produce organic material. The existence of this pathway does not mean every organism can perform it. Many larger animals depend on microbes either directly or through food webs. The conditions can vary sharply over distances of just a few metres.
turns.meaning_vi: Miệng phun thủy nhiệt có vi sinh vật dùng hóa tổng hợp thay cho ánh sáng.

turns.text_en: Certain animals depend on a close symbiotic relationship with microbes that live inside or on their bodies. Tube worms, for instance, have specialised arrangements for obtaining resources from their environment. Another local challenge is temperature variation, because the water near a hot fluid stream can differ sharply from the surrounding deep ocean. Organisms must respond to these gradients, and researchers cannot assume that a sample collected a short distance away represents the same conditions.
turns.meaning_vi: Quan hệ cộng sinh và nhiệt độ thay đổi mạnh tạo nên môi trường đặc biệt.

turns.text_en: To observe the habitat, scientists often use a remotely operated vehicle carrying cameras and sampling tools. Direct access is restricted by the extreme water pressure at great depth. A video recording can document behaviour without removing organisms, while a physical sample enables chemical or genetic work but may disturb the site. Each research method has a different cost and impact, so investigators plan their sampling carefully.
turns.meaning_vi: Robot điều khiển từ xa và áp suất nước là các yếu tố cốt lõi khi khảo sát.

turns.text_en: The chemistry of the vent fluid can change over time, affecting the supply of dissolved sulphide used by some microbes. Researchers also study the shape of mineral deposits known as chimney structures, which can grow or break apart. These changes alter the distribution of suitable habitats. An area that once hosted many organisms may become less active, while new sites appear elsewhere. The ecological picture is therefore dynamic rather than permanently fixed.
turns.meaning_vi: Nồng độ sulphide và cấu trúc ống khói khoáng thay đổi theo hoạt động địa chất.

turns.text_en: When comparing vents, scientists examine species diversity rather than counting only the largest animals visible on camera. They also consider habitat disturbance caused by sampling, tourism proposals or industrial activity. Because many species remain poorly understood, decisions about protection must account for uncertainty. A conservative survey plan can preserve a location for future research while still allowing carefully selected measurements of the processes taking place there.
turns.meaning_vi: Đa dạng loài và mức độ xáo trộn môi trường cần được tính tới trong bảo tồn.

turns.text_en: Deep environments are also difficult to revisit. Weather, ship time and equipment costs can limit observations to brief windows. A species seen once may not be absent on the next visit; it may simply be difficult to detect. Responsible studies therefore describe uncertainty and avoid claiming complete knowledge of a poorly sampled habitat.
turns.meaning_vi: Nêu giới hạn, ví dụ ứng dụng và ý nghĩa thực tế.

turns.text_en: These deep communities demonstrate that biological productivity can be based on chemical energy. Studying them requires a combination of geology, chemistry, engineering and ecological restraint.
turns.meaning_vi: Tổng kết và lưu ý cách diễn giải bằng chứng.
